site.title: Mario Madersbacher · Security Researcher
site.description: Security researcher and web penetration tester (HTB CWES) from Tyrol, Austria. Three CVEs, merged fixes in Impacket, Scapy, Volatility 3 and ffuf, accepted bug bounty reports. Everything on the page links to where you can check it.

person.name: Mario Madersbacher
person.headline: Security researcher and web penetration tester
person.intro: I find bugs in software people actually use. npm packages, the tools this field runs on, web apps in bug bounty programs. Then I report them so they get fixed. I'm still in school, Matura is in June 2027.
person.principle: I don't inflate severity. If there is a CVSS score on this page I demonstrated it, I didn't estimate it.

cves.mechanism: ReDoS in the regex that pulls IPv6 hosts out of a URL, reachable through the default `anchorme()` call. A URL under 100 bytes makes it backtrack exponentially and the Node.js event loop just stops.
cves.status: No fix released as of October 2026, npm latest is still 3.0.8.
cves.credit: Credited under my real name on the CVE record.

cves.mechanism: The address parser in `lib/addressparser` goes quadratic on comment-joined addresses. Through **mailparser** that is reachable from outside with a normal inbound mail, no auth, and the event loop stalls for seconds.
cves.status: Reported through a GitHub private advisory with a PoC and a fix suggestion. The maintainer patched it in 10.0.5.
cves.credit: Credited on the advisory and on the CVE record.

cves.mechanism: The `case_name` request parameter goes straight into `os.system()` in `py/web.py` (`controller_listen` and `controller_recover`), nothing is sanitised.
cves.status: The vendor never answered, so it went out through VulDB.

contributions.what: If `parallel` came from a config file, every run died with an unwrap panic (#1321). Fix plus a regression test, Rust.
Made the test suite pass on Windows. Three separate causes, one of them a pipe buffer deadlock in the stdout capture that only ever showed up as a hang.
The BGP NLRI dissector crashed when the prefix on the wire was shorter than the mask said.
`IP6ListField` crashed on a truncated last IPv6 address. That field sits in about 17 dissectors, DHCPv6, ICMPv6 and SRv6 among them.
`BootpDecoder` threw `struct.error` on BOOTP messages below the 300 octets RFC 1542 requires (#1900). Now handled the way the RFC says, with regression tests.
Entry for Vssadmin.exe deleting shadow copies (MITRE T1490).
NSH MD-Type 2 context headers didn't dissect at all, `count_from` had been given a string. Redone along RFC 8300 with real length handling.
OPC DA: `STDOBJREF.IPID` and `OpcDaFack.selack` used field classes where packet classes belong, so dissecting them raised `TypeError`.
Bluetooth `Set_Extended_Advertise_Enable` always returned a single advertising set, no matter what `num_sets` said.
The capabilities plugin broke on Linux kernels before 6.3. Fixed the structure handling.
An architecture typo blocked `scheduled_tasks` on 32-bit memory images.
Template for CVE-2020-10204 (Nexus Repository Manager 3 RCE), verified against a live instance.
NBNS name query responses only gave back the first address record. Now every entry gets parsed.
Detection rule for Kerberos pre-auth getting disabled on a user account, which is exactly what AS-REP roasting needs.

items.what: An unauthenticated third-party proxy endpoint at a big European electronics retailer. It exposed around 9.1 M customer trade-in records, name, IMEI, contact, payout, across seven EU storefronts.
An internal Confluence that let anonymous users in (resolved). SQL injection in a public geo API (accepted). An open Grafana/Mimir/Loki stack with tenant enumeration (closed as informational).
My first one, an XSS chain on an Austrian price comparison site.

bullets: Rolled out endpoints and printers across the hospital sites.
Network troubleshooting in a NAC and central DHCP environment.

Ran the Wazuh SIEM. Wrote about 20 custom Active Directory detection rules (DCSync, Kerberoasting, privileged group changes, MITRE T1098) with SID-based escalation and verified every one of them live.
Dug through a 35 M event index, found the cause of a KDC event storm (RC4/AES mismatch) and of MS-SQL and pass-the-hash false positives. Alert noise dropped by about 90 %.
CIS baseline and vulnerability assessments on the domain controllers. Escalated unpatched critical CVEs, among them an RD Licensing RCE at CVSS 9.8.
Designed the log retention (90 days hot, 12 months of snapshots) and wrote the SIEM operations handbook. Put about 700 assets into Snipe-IT with a script. VLANs on HPE Aruba Instant On switches.
